lines.narration: Neela walks into the garage with a tear still drying on her cheek, and Sean reads her face without either of them saying a word. He doesn't need the sentence. He can see it.
Across town, the white suit and panama hat belong to Kamata, the uncle DK has been going to see. Takashi hands over the week's take and the old man sits down to the books.

Kamata works the printouts and admits he doesn't understand half of what he's looking at. Takashi laughs it off — it's more complicated than it looks. Then the smile dies, because the old man just sits there, silent, and keeps reading.
In a blue-lit office the accusation lands: Han, the partner Takashi fronts this whole operation with, has been taking money out of the books. Takashi doesn't deny it. He drops his eyes.
Being robbed by your own partner, and hearing it from the uncle who reads your ledgers better than you do, is a humiliation paid for in public.

Kamata turns it into a proverb — for want of a nail the shoe was lost, and the war with it — then lifts a framed picture off the desk and leaves Takashi doubled over it. The thing you overlook is how everything above it comes down.

Takashi drives straight to the garage, Morimoto behind him. He hauls Han out from under the lift, shouts about the side deals, and slams him into the tyre racks. The whole crew watches, Sean included, and nobody moves.

claim.subject: the man in the black shirt

lines.narration: The pistol comes up into Han's face. Han answers the way he'd answer a late invoice — Takashi would still be shaking down tea houses for chump change if it wasn't for him. True. Also the worst thing he could have said.

Han bolts the bay in a shower of sparks and the crew pours into the street after him. Sean goes too, Neela beside him, in the red Evo Han handed over for nothing — which tells you who he's driving for.
Han runs flat out through the tunnels, slicing between cars faster than the traffic can register. He once called Tokyo his Mexico — the place he'd stopped running to. Tonight he's running again.
Inside the Evo, Neela has stopped watching the road. She grew up in Takashi's grandmother's house — of everyone in these cars, she alone knows both men well enough to know neither will stop.
Then the road ahead fills with people. They drive straight into the packed crossing anyway, nosing bodies aside at speed. Nobody lifts off the throttle.
Han slings the orange car broadside across a lit junction and threads head-on past an oncoming sedan, and for a few seconds it looks like he gets out of this the way he's got out of everything else.

The orange car cartwheels down the avenue and lands upside down against a kerb, one wheel rolling clear. Han is trapped inside and does not move. Sean sprints for him and is still running when it detonates.

Takashi watches the fire, then drives away and leaves Sean and Neela in the firelight. Sean's face does the arithmetic in two seconds — he came here to race for fun, and the bill for all of it just landed on somebody else.

claim.subject: the man in the black shirt

lines.narration: Takashi is waiting in the dark lane outside the house. He twists a hand into Sean's collar and puts a pistol to his head — and Sean's father, the naval officer, steps out with his own gun up. Neither man lowers it.

claim.subject: the man in the black henley

lines.narration: Neela breaks the standoff. She's the only thing in that lane Takashi actually wants, so she goes with him to get the gun off Sean's head. Nobody says the terms aloud. Takashi gets Neela; Sean keeps his head.
In the alley his father tries to take it off him — I'm your father, I'm responsible for my own mess. Sean won't have it. I did this, he says. I can't run away from it.

claim.subject: the older man in the olive jacket

lines.narration: His father presses him to get out of Tokyo while there's still a plane he can be put on, and Sean's face closes like a door. He doesn't answer. He walks off down the dark street, working on the only move he has left.

claim.subject: the grey-haired man in the olive jacket
